channel.title: Nature Cell Biology
channel.description: Nature Cell Biology publishes peer-reviewed original research of the highest quality in all areas of cell biology with an emphasis on studies that provide insights into the molecular mechanisms underlying cellular processes. The journal’s scope is broad and ranges from cytoskeletal dynamics, membrane transport, adhesion and migration, cell division, signalling pathways, development and stem cells, to molecular and cellular mechanisms underlying cancer. Nature Cell Biology provides timely and informative coverage of cell biological advances.

item.title: Mitochondria contact lipid droplets through the mitochondrial import complex binding to lipid metabolism enzyme Ayr1
item.content:encoded:
Nature Cell Biology, Published online: 26 February 2026; doi:10.1038/s41556-026-01890-3

Heinen et al. show that the mitochondrial import complex recruits lipid droplets to the mitochondrial outer membrane. The mitochondrial import complex binds to the lipid metabolism enzyme Ayr1 and contributes to lipid-droplet biogenesis and homeostasis.
item.dc:title: Mitochondria contact lipid droplets through the mitochondrial import complex binding to lipid metabolism enzyme Ayr1

item.title: PML targets and resolves structured protein inclusions to mitigate neurodegeneration
item.content:encoded:
Nature Cell Biology, Published online: 25 February 2026; doi:10.1038/s41556-026-01894-z

Wang et al. show that promyelocytic leukaemia protein (PML) reduces polyG inclusions via chaperone-mediated disaggregation and proteasome-dependent degradation. This suggests a possible role for PML in various neurodegenerative diseases.
item.dc:title: PML targets and resolves structured protein inclusions to mitigate neurodegeneration

item.title: LBR and LAP2 mediate heterochromatin tethering to the nuclear periphery to preserve genome homeostasis
item.content:encoded:
Nature Cell Biology, Published online: 24 February 2026; doi:10.1038/s41556-025-01822-7

Lewis et al. identify lamin B receptor (LBR) and lamina-associated polypeptide 2 (LAP2) as major factors that tether heterochromatin to the envelope. Deletion of these proteins causes changes in 3D genome organization, gene expression and cell fate determination.
item.dc:title: LBR and LAP2 mediate heterochromatin tethering to the nuclear periphery to preserve genome homeostasis

item.title: Cellular mechanisms of brain lipid metabolism in health and disease
item.content:encoded:
Nature Cell Biology, Published online: 20 February 2026; doi:10.1038/s41556-026-01880-5

This Review discusses brain lipid metabolism from a cellular perspective, focusing on lipid uptake, de novo synthesis, storage, breakdown and intercellular transfer, and highlights its emerging implications for brain health and disease.
item.dc:title: Cellular mechanisms of brain lipid metabolism in health and disease

item.title: Peritumoural adipose tissue drives immune evasion in colorectal cancer via adipose–mesenchymal transformation
item.content:encoded:
Nature Cell Biology, Published online: 19 February 2026; doi:10.1038/s41556-026-01885-0

Wang, Zheng, Qian, Pan, Tian et al. characterize the crosstalk between peritumoural visceral adipose tissue and colorectal tumour microenvironment and report an immune escape mechanism, which may be potentially targeted for improved immunotherapy.
item.dc:title: Peritumoural adipose tissue drives immune evasion in colorectal cancer via adipose–mesenchymal transformation

item.title: Adaptor-mediated recruitment of three dyneins to dynactin enhances force generation
item.content:encoded:
Nature Cell Biology, Published online: 16 February 2026; doi:10.1038/s41556-026-01877-0

Dynein–dynactin–cargo adaptor complexes typically function with two dynein motors. Rao et al. show that, under mechanical load, these complexes can recruit a third dynein via a second adaptor, increasing force generation.
item.dc:title: Adaptor-mediated recruitment of three dyneins to dynactin enhances force generation
